comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 Teaching and Examination Regulations, checked 2026-09-25
comparator.route: General Artificial Intelligence pathway without an optional specialisation
comparator.sourceNotes: For the general 2026–27 pathway, the TER lists 54 EC of compulsory first-year units plus one 6-EC restricted choice (first-listed Information Management); 42 EC of compulsory second-year units plus three 6-EC restricted choices (first-listed Robot Interaction, Data Structures and Algorithms for AI, AI in Health); and 24 EC compulsory third-year project, ethics and research-design units plus one 6-EC restricted choice (first-listed Cognitive Psychology for AI) and 30 EC genuinely open academic minor/profiling space. The zero-credit language test is excluded. This broad coherent 180-EC route has no optional specialisation credential. The TER permits incoming 2026–27 students to opt into Intelligent Systems or Socially Aware Computing under transitional rules, which are not required for this generic target. Every selected restricted choice is one valid unit; other listed options are not combined or presented as mandatory.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three conceptually distinct, evidenced UCR curricula pass the 24-course and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates: broad hybrid intelligence and cognition, technical AI system construction, and health/behaviour applications. The energy-systems interest is a separate application direction but the approved maximum of three alternatives is already reached; the isolated teaching direction lacks a specific UCR teacher-education sequence.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study how intelligent systems solve problems and choose actions; UCR focuses on formal planning.
Both cover logical and discrete structures for AI reasoning.
Both address computational learning and intelligent decisions; UCR specialises in reinforcement learning rather than the entire VU unit.
Both address structuring, storing and querying knowledge or information; UCR concentrates on relational databases.
Both teach algorithm design and data structures relevant to efficient AI implementation.
Both teach foundational programming for constructing AI software, with UCR using Python.
No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Computational thinking unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.

No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Project Intelligent Systems unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.
No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Information Management unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.

No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Bachelor project Artificial Intelligence unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.
Both teach machine-learning methods and their evaluation.
Both address robotics and interaction; UCR surveys broader robotic systems rather than a dedicated HRI project.
Both develop linear algebra needed for AI, though UCR does not cover the full calculus component in this row.
Both study probability, statistical inference and uncertainty.

No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Introduction to Artificial Intelligence unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.
No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Text Mining for AI unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.

No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Open academic elective space / minor unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.
Both cultivate academic writing and reflection; UCR combines this with broader personal and professional development.
Both examine normative and societal responsibilities of AI systems.
Both investigate cognition relevant to AI; UCR focuses on higher-order brain functions.
Both introduce human psychology and cognition; the UCR course frames brain and behaviour broadly.
Both study the behaviour of people in social situations; UCR does not claim the same computational modelling component.
Both teach how to design and assess empirical studies; UCR applies this to experimental psychology rather than AI research specifically.

No selected UCR course directly covers the VU Human-Computer Interaction for AI unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.
No selected UCR course directly covers the VU History of AI unit at a comparable subject or educational-function level; the required or choice component is retained with its full credits.

notes.text: VU requires a structured AI sequence, restricted choices, a 15-EC independent bachelor project and a 30-EC open minor. UCR can assemble substantial AI, data, cognition and ethics study across its open curriculum but does not reproduce each VU AI project or its mandatory individual research project. Health applications at UCR combine domain study with general AI methods rather than a dedicated clinical AI training unit.
